# Biking Geek — Copilot Instructions

## Project Overview

Biking Geek is a Jekyll-based blog focused on cycling and sports: bike computers, mountain bikes, cycling gear, protective equipment, and sports accessories. Published via GitHub Pages at `sports.geeknite.com` using the custom theme `FerranSalguero/geeknite-theme`.

**Important**: This is the cycling/sports content spin-off from GeekNite. Biking Geek focuses exclusively on cycling, mountain biking, and sports-related gear reviews and guides.

---

## Key Architecture Decisions

### Content Structure
- **Posts**: `_posts/YYYY-MM-DD-title.md` with YAML frontmatter (title, date, tags, description, excerpt)
- **Multilingual**: Content in both English and Spanish (Castellano). Check `locale` in frontmatter
- **Cross-linking**: Heavy use of Jekyll's `{%- post_url -%}` tag for internal references (3–5 minimum per post)
- **Affiliate Focus**: Product reviews with Amazon affiliate links via `site.constants.wsib` and regional Amazon tags

### Custom Theme & Configuration
- Remote theme: `FerranSalguero/geeknite-theme` (Minimal Mistakes fork)
- Configuration: `_config.yml` defines critical constants for Amazon affiliate tags (`amazon_es`, `amazon_com`, `amazon_uk`, `amazon_de`, `amazon_fr`, `amazon_it`)
- Timezone: `Europe/Madrid`
- Permalinks: `/:year/:month/:title:output_ext`
- All posts auto-configured with: TOC, sticky TOC, author profile, sidebar nav `top-posts`
- Markdown: Kramdown with GFM input
- Windows dev environment assumed (PowerShell scripts, backslash paths)

### SEO Configuration
- **Google Analytics**: `G-TMNY7YNW2F` via `_config.yml`
- **Google AdSense**: `ca-pub-2992269112655291` loaded in `_includes/head/custom.html`
- **Google Site Verification**: configured in `_config.yml`
- **Open Graph default image**: `og_image` set in `_config.yml` for social sharing
- **Fallback teaser**: `/assets/images/general.jpg` for archive listings without images
- **Sitemap**: Auto-generated by `jekyll-sitemap` plugin, referenced in `robots.txt`
- **robots.txt**: Custom file with Jekyll front matter, allows all crawlers and points to sitemap

### Performance Optimizations
The site uses several performance optimizations configured in `_includes/head/custom.html` and `assets/css/custom.scss`:

**Resource Hints** (`_includes/head/custom.html`):
- `preconnect` to critical origins: `i.imgur.com`, `m.media-amazon.com`, `googletagmanager.com`, `pagead2.googlesyndication.com`
- `dns-prefetch` for less critical origins: `one-link.amazon.com`, `amazon.com`, `amazon.es`, `cdn.jsdelivr.net`

**Image Optimization**:
- All images use `loading="lazy"` for deferred loading
- Amazon product images have explicit `width="120" height="120"` to prevent layout shift
- Images use `decoding="async"` for non-blocking decode
- CSS enforces `height: auto; max-width: 100%` on content images

**CSS Performance** (`assets/css/custom.scss`):
- Amazon image cells use `aspect-ratio: 1/1; object-fit: contain`
- Archive items use `content-visibility: auto; contain-intrinsic-size: 0 120px` for rendering performance on long lists

**Third-Party Scripts**:
- Amazon OneLink loaded with `async`
- Google AdSense loaded with `async`

## Amazon Affiliate Integration

**Critical**: All product mentions must link to `{{ site.constants.wsib }}` — maximize affiliate linking throughout content.

### Product Linking Strategy
- Link EVERY cycling product mention (bike computers, bikes, gear, helmets, saddles, pedals) to `{{ site.constants.wsib }}`
- Use inline text links: `[Garmin Edge 530]({{ site.constants.wsib }}garmin edge 530)`
- For specific Amazon storefronts, use regional constants: `{{ site.constants.amazon_com }}`, `{{ site.constants.amazon_es }}`, etc.
- Prioritize visual product tables over plain text links when possible

### Amazon Product Tables
Use `_includes/amazon.html` for multi-region product tables showing the same ASIN across 6 Amazon regions (US, UK, DE, ES, FR, IT):
```markdown
{% include amazon.html asin="B09XX5FVHJ" imageUrl="https://i.imgur.com/xxxxxm.jpg" title="Garmin Edge 540" %}
```
Parameters:
- `asin` (required): Amazon product ASIN
- `imageUrl` (required): Product image URL (Imgur with `m` suffix or Amazon CDN)
- `title` (optional): Product name — used for alt text on images. Defaults to "Product"

The component automatically generates affiliate links with the correct tag for each region, uses `rel="nofollow sponsored"`, lazy loading, and explicit image dimensions.

## Post Creation & Editing

### Post Creation Pattern
1. Create file: `_posts/YYYY-MM-DD-descriptive-slug.md`
2. Add comprehensive frontmatter:
   ```yaml
   ---
   title: "Product Name: Catchy Review Title"
   date: YYYY-MM-DD
   tags: [cycling, gear, brand, product-type]
   description: "SEO-optimized description 150-160 chars in post language"
   excerpt: "Longer excerpt for social sharing"
   last_modified_at: 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS+01:00'
   redirect_from:  # Optional, only for URL migrations
     - /old/path.html
   hero_image: "AI image generation prompt if no real image available"
   ---
   ```
3. Add **hero image** at top (see Hero Image section below)
4. Add 3–5 internal `post_url` links to related existing posts throughout the content
5. Link ALL product mentions to `{{ site.constants.wsib }}`
6. Add `{% include amazon.html %}` product tables for major items
7. Add **Related Posts** section at the end with 3–5 `post_url` links
8. **Always update `last_modified_at`** when editing any post

### Hero Image
Must follow this format with affiliate link and alignment:
```markdown
[![Product Name](IMAGE_URL){: .align-right}]({{ site.constants.wsib }}Product Name)
```
- Always include `{: .align-right}` for proper text wrapping alongside content
- Wrap in affiliate link using `{{ site.constants.wsib }}`

**Image Sourcing (in order of preference):**

1. **Amazon product images** (preferred for product reviews) — copy the image URL directly from the Amazon product listing:
   ```
   https://m.media-amazon.com/images/I/XXXXXXXXX._AC_SX425_.jpg
   ```
2. **Imgur hosting** — for images from manufacturer sites or other sources, upload to Imgur and use the medium size `m` suffix:
   ```
   https://i.imgur.com/xxxxxm.jpg
   ```
   - **Note**: Uploading to Imgur requires user intervention (Copilot cannot upload images)
3. **Fallback image** — when no suitable product image exists, use `/assets/images/general.jpg` AND add a `hero_image` field in frontmatter with a descriptive AI image generation prompt:
   ```yaml
   hero_image: "Mountain biker riding on a forest trail, dynamic action shot, natural lighting, green trees, cycling gear visible, vibrant colors, professional photography, 16:9"
   ```
   - Adapt the prompt based on content: MTB trails, road cycling, gear flat-lay, etc.
   - The user will later generate the image with an AI tool and upload it to Imgur
4. **No image** — only acceptable for non-product editorial posts (e.g., opinion pieces, safety tips). Still add a `hero_image` prompt in frontmatter so an image can be added later

**CRITICAL**:
- Never invent Imgur URLs — always verify the image exists by checking with `fetch_webpage` or using existing URLs from the blog
- Never use broken or placeholder image URLs

### Internal Linking Convention
**Critical**: When linking between posts, use Jekyll's `post_url` tag:
```markdown
[link text]({%- post_url 2023-07-06-garmin-edge-540-review -%})
```
- No file extension
- Include full date prefix (YYYY-MM-DD)
- Hyphens only (no spaces)
- Use `{%-` syntax (with dash) to strip whitespace for cleaner HTML output

### ⚠️ CRITICAL: Avoiding post_url Errors
**NEVER invent post_url references.** Before adding any `post_url` tag:

1. **ALWAYS verify the post exists** by running:
   ```powershell
   Get-ChildItem "_posts" -Filter "*keyword*" | Select-Object Name
   ```
2. **Use the EXACT filename** including the correct date (e.g., `2023-08-22` not `2023-08-15`)
3. **If no matching post exists**, use an affiliate link instead:
   ```markdown
   # WRONG — post doesn't exist
   [Garmin Edge 840]({%- post_url 2025-06-15-garmin-edge-840-review -%})

   # CORRECT — use affiliate link when post doesn't exist
   [Garmin Edge 840]({{ site.constants.wsib }}Garmin Edge 840)
   ```
4. **Never use future dates** for posts that don't exist yet
5. **Common mistakes to avoid:**
   - Wrong date: `2023-07-05-garmin-edge-540...` vs actual `2023-07-06-garmin-edge-540...`
   - Invented slugs: `best-budget-gps-2025` when no such post exists
   - Missing suffixes: `igpsport-bsc300-review` vs actual `igpsport-bsc300-review-smart-affordable-bike-sensor`

## Content Guidelines

### Post Structure
1. **Hero image** at top with affiliate link and `.align-right` (see Hero Image section)
2. **Intro** (1–2 sentences) — frame a decision, NOT "here are some great products" but "if you need X, here's what to buy"
3. **Quick Answer** — give the verdict immediately for users who want fast answers
4. **H2 sections** for major topics (Design, Performance, Battery Life, etc.)
5. **H3 subsections** for specific features/aspects — link each product to `{{ site.constants.wsib }}`
6. **Amazon product tables** with `{% include amazon.html %}` for featured products
7. **Decision table** — summary table at the end with affiliate links
8. **Related Posts section** — 3–5 `post_url` links at the end (use `## Related Posts` or `## Posts Relacionados`)

### Monetization-First Content Strategy

**CRITICAL**: Every post must follow this user journey:
```
User arrives with a specific question
    → Reads content
    → Makes a decision
    → Clicks affiliate link
```

**Content Philosophy:**
- **DO NOT "recommend things"** — Instead, **SOLVE DECISIONS**
- User searches with a specific problem → Post provides the answer → User clicks to buy
- Every section must lead to an actionable decision with a clear affiliate link
- Avoid generic "top 10 lists" — Focus on "Which X should I buy for Y situation?"

**Post Types That Convert:**

| Post Type | Example Title | Why It Works |
|-----------|---------------|--------------|
| Decision resolver | "Garmin Edge 530 vs 540: Which Should You Buy?" | User has a specific choice to make |
| Problem solver | "Best MTB Suspension Fork Under €300 for Trail Riding" | User has budget + use case |
| Comparison | "iGPSPORT BSC300 vs BSC300T: Complete Budget Bike Computer Guide" | User deciding between options |
| Buying guide | "Which Bike Computer to Buy in 2025?" | User ready to purchase |

**Post Structure for Conversion:**
1. **Title**: Frame as a decision/question the user needs answered
2. **Intro**: Acknowledge the user's specific problem (1–2 sentences max)
3. **Quick Answer**: Give the verdict immediately for users who want fast answers
4. **Detailed Analysis**: For users who want to understand why
5. **Decision Table**: Summary table at the end with affiliate links
6. **Single CTA**: One clear "buy now" action per section

**Avoid These Patterns:**
- "Here are 10 great products you should try"
- "I recommend checking out..."
- Generic product lists without decision context
- Long intros before getting to the point
- Multiple CTAs that confuse the user

**Use These Patterns:**
- "If you want X, buy [Product A](affiliate). If you need Y, get [Product B](affiliate)."
- "The verdict: [Product](affiliate) is the best choice for [specific use case]."
- Tables with clear winner indicators and affiliate links
- "Bottom line: Buy [this](affiliate) if... Buy [that](affiliate) if..."

### Tone & Style
- **Professional and informative** with enthusiastic touch
- Avoid overly casual or humorous tone (no "Welcome!", "Hey cyclists!", etc.)
- Focus on product details, comparisons, and value propositions
- **Budget-Focused**: Emphasizes value for amateur cyclists/users
- **Bilingual**: English primary, some Spanish posts (check `locale` in frontmatter)
- Product comparisons and "vs" reviews with winner declarations per section

### Content Quality & Rigor
- **Fact-check all data**: Never invent specifications, prices, or product details
- **Be rigorous**: Verify technical specs, release dates, and product features
- **Long-form content**: Posts must be 2000+ words with genuinely informative and useful content — not filler. Cover every relevant angle: specs, comparisons, use cases, pros/cons, alternatives, buying advice, and related context
- If uncertain about a detail, research it or omit it rather than guessing
- Use precise measurements, accurate model numbers, and verified information

## Common Tasks

### Updating Product Links
When a post becomes outdated, create a new post and update ALL references:
```powershell
# Find all references to old post
Select-String -Path "_posts\*.md" -Pattern "2023-07-04-prime-day-bike-gadgets"
```
Then replace with new `post_url` tag across affected files.

### Top Posts Navigation
When a post is comprehensive, high-quality, and likely to drive traffic, add it to `_data/navigation.yml` under `top-posts`:
```yaml
top-posts:
  - title: "Top posts"
    children:
      - title: "Post Title"
        url: /YYYY/MM/slug.html
```
- URL format follows the permalink pattern: `/:year/:month/:title.html`
- Keep the list curated — only high-traffic or evergreen content

### Reviewing Existing Posts Checklist
When reviewing/editing a published post, follow this checklist:
1. **Frontmatter**: Ensure `last_modified_at` is set to current date, `description` exists (150–160 chars), and `tags` are relevant
2. **Hero image**: Must exist with `{: .align-right}` and affiliate link wrapper. If using fallback image, add `hero_image` prompt in frontmatter
3. **Tone**: Must be professional, decision-focused — rewrite casual/enthusiastic intros
4. **Affiliate links**: ALL product mentions must link to `{{ site.constants.wsib }}` — add missing ones
5. **Internal links**: Add 3–5 `post_url` references to related existing posts (verify each exists first)
6. **Amazon product tables**: Add `{% include amazon.html %}` for major products with ASINs and `title` parameter
7. **Encoding**: Fix any broken characters (mojibake like `Ã³` → `ó`, `Ã±` → `ñ`, `â€"` → `—`)
8. **Related posts section**: Must exist at end with 3–5 `post_url` links
9. **Decision table**: Add summary table with affiliate links at the end if missing
10. **Top posts**: If quality is high enough, add to `_data/navigation.yml` under `top-posts`

## Domain-Specific Notes

### Bike Computers & GPS
- Garmin Edge series (500, 520, 530, 540, 1040, etc.)
- iGPSPORT models (iGS630, BSC300, BSC300T, BSC200S, iGS800, etc.)
- Other brands: Wahoo ELEMNT, SRAM Karoo, Magene C606, TwoNav Terra
- Comparison reviews with feature-by-feature winners
- **Link every bike computer mention to `{{ site.constants.wsib }}`**

### Mountain Bikes & Components
- Full bike reviews (hardtail, full suspension)
- Frame geometry and suspension analysis
- Component reviews (forks, shocks, wheels, saddles, dropper posts, grips)
- Brand coverage: Canyon, Mondraker, Santa Cruz, YT, Production Privee, etc.
- **Every bike/component must have Amazon affiliate link when available**

### Cycling Gear & Protective Equipment
- Helmets (Bluegrass Rogue, Bell Super DH, Fox, etc.)
- Knee pads and protective gear (Fox Launch Pro, etc.)
- Clothing reviews (jerseys, shorts, socks, gloves, jackets)
- Shoes (Five Ten Sleuth, etc.) and pedals
- Sunglasses (Tifosi Seek, BBB Impress, Adidas Evil Eye, etc.)
- **Link all gear to Amazon or manufacturer affiliate**

### Sports Accessories
- Running watches and fitness trackers (Garmin Forerunner, Huawei Fit, Amazfit)
- Saddles and bike fit equipment (Selle Italia)
- Hydration gear (Osprey, Dakine backpacks)
- Indoor trainers (Minoura, CycleOps Fluid2, Elite, Zwift)
- Bike lights (Nitefighter BT21/BT40s, budget comparison roundups)

### Spanish Language Content
- Some posts in Spanish (check frontmatter for `locale`)
- Common Spanish cycling terms: bicicleta, ciclismo, ruedas, suspensión, tija, cubierta
- Use `## Posts Relacionados` instead of `## Related Posts` for Spanish posts
- Use `## Donde Comprar` instead of `## Where to Buy` for Spanish posts
- Watch for UTF-8 encoding issues with Spanish characters (ñ, á, é, í, ó, ú)

### Comparison Posts Pattern
Structure: Intro → Feature-by-feature → Winner per section → Final verdict → Decision table with affiliate links → Related posts

## AI Assistant Constraints
- **Vision is NOT enabled** for this organization. Never attempt image analysis, screenshot reading, or any vision-based operations. Error: `{"message":"vision is not enabled for this organization","code":""}`. If image content is needed, ask the user to describe it.
- Follow instructions strictly — do not attempt unsupported features.

## Pitfalls to Avoid
1. **Never** use file extensions in `post_url` tags
2. **Always** check `_config.yml` constants before hardcoding affiliate links
3. **Always** update `last_modified_at` when editing posts
4. When linking to posts, verify the exact filename (dates matter!)
5. Imgur image URLs should use the `m` suffix for medium size: `https://i.imgur.com/xxxxxm.jpg`
6. **Never invent** product specifications — verify all technical data
7. **Encoding**: Watch for UTF-8 mojibake with Spanish characters (ñ, á, é) — fix immediately when found
8. **Length**: Aim for 2000+ words of useful content for SEO depth
9. **SEO**: Optimize titles and descriptions with exclusive and original content
10. **Never** use `redirect_to` pointing to the same post — only use redirects for URL migrations from old paths
11. **Never invent** Imgur URLs or `post_url` references — always verify they exist first
12. **Always** include the `title` parameter in `{% include amazon.html %}` for proper alt text

## Debugging

### Build Errors
- Check YAML frontmatter syntax (common issue: unescaped colons in titles — wrap in quotes)
- Verify `post_url` references exist (wrong date/slug breaks build)
- Windows paths: Use forward slashes in Jekyll configs

### Encoding Fixes
**Common Problem**: UTF-8 corruption (mojibake) from CP1252 double-encoding.

Characters like `â€™` (should be `'`), `â€"` (should be `—`), `Ã³` (should be `ó`), `Ã±` (should be `ñ`) appear when UTF-8 multi-byte sequences are re-interpreted as Windows-1252.

Search regex: `â€™|â€"|Ã³|Ã±|Ã¡|Ã©|Ãº`

Always check and fix encoding when editing old posts. Spanish characters (ñ, á, é, í, ó, ú) are particularly affected.

### Theme Issues
Remote theme changes require cache clear. Delete `.jekyll-metadata` and `_site/` for fresh build.
